entities.name: Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustum
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustum was a pivotal figure in the early 8th-century Islamic world, leading the Rustamud Imamate in the Maghreb region of North Africa.

Born in present-day Iraq around 720 CE, he rose to prominence as a missionary and politician, shaping the region's politics and leaving a lasting legacy.

The Rustamud Imamate, established by ibn Rustum, played a significant role in the history of the Maghreb, influencing the development of Islamic law and governance in the region.

As a key player in the early Islamic period, ibn Rustum's actions had far-reaching consequences, shaping the trajectory of Islamic civilization and leaving a lasting impact on the region.

The intricacies of his life and reign continue to captivate historians and scholars, providing valuable insights into the complexities of early Islamic society.
